papers.title: Bayesian Optimization for Synthetic Gene Design
papers.abstract: We address the problem of synthetic gene design using Bayesian optimization. The main issue when designing a gene is that the design space is defined in terms of long strings of characters of different lengths, which renders the optimization intractable. We propose a three-step approach to deal with this issue. First, we use a Gaussian process model to emulate the behavior of the cell. As inputs of the model, we use a set of biologically meaningful gene features, which allows us to define optimal gene designs rules. Based on the model outputs we define a multi-task acquisition function to optimize simultaneously severals aspects of interest. Finally, we define an evaluation function, which allow us to rank sets of candidate gene sequences that are coherent with the optimal design strategy. We illustrate the performance of this approach in a real gene design experiment with mammalian cells.

summary_en.motivation: To efficiently design synthetic genes by addressing the intractably large search space of DNA sequences.
summary_en.method: A Gaussian process surrogate model is built with biologically meaningful features, and a multi-task acquisition function optimizes multiple design objectives simultaneously.
summary_en.result: The proposed three-step Bayesian optimization approach successfully generates optimal gene designs validated in a real mammalian cell experiment.
summary_en.validation: Experimental validation in mammalian cells demonstrates the practical viability of the optimization framework.
